principles: A victory won without the strength of the Lord

world_behind.title: He is made leader at fifteen
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives his size as the stated reason for making a fifteen-year-old the leader of the armies. Mormon 1:2 has Ammaron choose the same boy at ten for being quick to observe, so two men pick him for two unrelated qualities within five years.

world_behind.title: The account is a retreat
world_behind.text: Verses 4 through 6 lose Angola, the land of David, and fall back to Joshua.

world_behind.title: Samuel's prophecy is named as fulfilled
world_behind.text: Verse 10 says the people cried as Samuel the Lamanite had said they would (Hel. 13:32–33).

world_behind.title: He records his own hope and its collapse
world_behind.text: Verse 12 has his heart rejoice at the people's mourning and verse 13 calls that joy vain. 2 Corinthians 7:10 draws the same distinction between godly sorrow and the sorrow of the world; Mormon reaches it by being wrong first and recording the correction.

world_behind.title: He explains what he leaves out
world_behind.text: Verse 18 says the full account of the wickedness went on the plates of Nephi, and these hold less.

world_behind.title: He states the withdrawal plainly
world_behind.text: Verse 26 says the strength of the Lord was not with them even in a victory. Helaman 4:13 had explained an earlier defeat the same way, that they were left in their own strength; Mormon applies the formula to a battle his side won.

world_behind.title: The book ends its first phase in a treaty
world_behind.text: Verses 28 and 29 divide the land at the narrow passage, the Nephites taking everything northward. Alma 22:32 measures that neck at a day and a half's journey, and Ether 10:20 has the Jaredites building a great city there. The treaty line runs across the most-described feature in the volume's geography.

words.text: A complete turning over. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible not at all. Verse 8 uses it of blood and carnage across the whole land.
Loud grief, formal mourning. Treated at Mosiah 21:9. It appears eight times, twice in this chapter, in the record, and the King James Bible twenty-five.
Favor freely given. The record uses the word thirty-one times and the King James Bible one hundred and seventy. Verse 15 is the record's only use of the phrase "day of grace".
To hold back from doing something. Treated at Alma 20:18. The word turns up six times here, and the King James Bible twenty-two.
Steadiness under pressure. The record uses the word nine times, with none in the King James Bible. Verse 25 uses it of thirty thousand standing against fifty thousand.
Ruin, disaster. Its count is three times in this book, while the King James Bible nineteen. Verse 27 attaches it to his own sorrow.
A formal agreement between peoples. The record uses the word three times, while the King James Bible has none. Verse 28 has it made with the Lamanites and the robbers together.

phrases.term: Notwithstanding I being young, was large in stature
phrases.text: The qualification given for command. Size is the only reason the verse offers.

phrases.term: It was one complete revolution throughout all the face of the land
phrases.text: The scale stated in a single phrase. Verse 8 says the blood was on both sides.

phrases.term: No man could keep that which was his own
phrases.text: Samuel's curse described as daily experience. The prophecy is named in the same verse.

phrases.term: My heart did begin to rejoice within me
phrases.text: Mormon's hope, recorded as he felt it. Verse 13 will withdraw it.

phrases.term: Their sorrowing was not unto repentance
phrases.text: The distinction the chapter turns on. Verse 13 calls the other kind the sorrowing of the damned.

phrases.term: Because the Lord would not always suffer them to take happiness in sin
phrases.text: The reason the sorrow came at all. The grief is caused by the loss of the pleasure and not by the sin.

phrases.term: They did curse God, and wish to die
phrases.text: Despair without repentance. Job 2:9 puts the same two acts in one line.

phrases.term: I saw that the day of grace was passed with them
phrases.text: The verdict, temporal and spiritual. Verse 15 is the only place the record uses the phrase.

phrases.term: Heaped up as dung upon the face of the land
phrases.text: The image for thousands of dead. Jeremiah 9:22 uses it of an unburied army.

phrases.term: A continual scene of wickedness and abominations has been before mine eyes
phrases.text: His reason for leaving the full account off these plates. He has seen nothing else since he was old enough to understand.

phrases.term: Nevertheless the strength of the Lord was not with us
phrases.text: A victory reported and immediately qualified. Verse 26 says they had become weak like their brethren.

verses.label: v. 1–8
verses.title: Command and retreat
verses.text: That same year war begins again, and though Mormon is young he is large in stature, so the people of Nephi appoint him leader of their armies. In his sixteenth year he goes out at the head of an army, three hundred and twenty-six years having passed. The next year the Lamanites come with such power that his armies are frightened and will not fight, and they retreat north. They take the city of Angola and fortify it, but are driven out, and driven out of the land of David as well, and march to the land of Joshua by the west seashore. They gather their people into one body as fast as they can. The land is full of robbers and Lamanites, and despite the destruction hanging over them the people do not repent, so blood and carnage spread over the whole land on both sides.

verses.label: v. 9–11
verses.title: Aaron, and the mourning
verses.text: The Lamanite king Aaron comes with forty-four thousand and Mormon withstands him with forty-two thousand and beats him, and Aaron flees. Three hundred and thirty years have passed. The Nephites begin to repent of their iniquity and to cry as Samuel the prophet had said they would (Hel. 13:32–33), since no man could keep what was his own for the thieves and robbers and murderers and the magic art and witchcraft in the land. Mourning and lamentation begin everywhere, and especially among the people of Nephi.

verses.label: v. 12–15
verses.title: A hope withdrawn
verses.text: Seeing their lamentation and sorrow before the Lord, Mormon's heart begins to rejoice, since he knows the mercies and long-suffering of the Lord and supposes God will be merciful and they will become righteous again. His joy proves vain, because their sorrowing was not unto repentance but the sorrowing of the damned, since the Lord would not let them keep taking happiness in sin. They do not come to Jesus with broken hearts and contrite spirits; they curse God and wish to die, though they still struggle with the sword for their lives. His sorrow returns, and he sees the day of grace is past with them, temporally and spiritually, with thousands hewn down in open rebellion and heaped up as dung. Three hundred and forty-four years have passed.

verses.label: v. 16–19
verses.title: Jashon, and the plates
verses.text: In the three hundred and forty-fifth year the Nephites flee before the Lamanites until they reach the land of Jashon. The city of Jashon is near where Ammaron deposited the records, so Mormon goes according to Ammaron's word, takes the plates of Nephi, and makes a record as instructed. On the plates of Nephi he makes a full account of all the wickedness, but on these plates he holds back, since a continual scene of wickedness has been before his eyes since he was old enough to understand men. He says woe is him for their wickedness, that his heart has been filled with sorrow all his days, and that he knows he will be lifted up at the last day.

verses.label: v. 20–24
verses.title: Shem
verses.text: That year the people of Nephi are hunted and driven northward to the land called Shem. They fortify the city of Shem and gather in as many people as possible, hoping to save them. In the three hundred and forty-sixth year the Lamanites come again. Mormon speaks to his people and urges them with great energy to stand boldly and fight for their wives, their children, their houses, and their homes. His words rouse them somewhat, and they stand with boldness.

verses.label: v. 25–27
verses.title: A hollow victory
verses.text: Thirty thousand contend against fifty thousand and stand with such firmness that the Lamanites flee. They pursue and beat them again, but the strength of the Lord is not with them; they are left to themselves, the Spirit does not abide in them, and they have become weak like their brethren. Mormon's heart sorrows because of this great calamity, and they go on against the Lamanites and the robbers of Gadianton until they retake the lands of their inheritance.

verses.label: v. 28–29
verses.title: The treaty
verses.text: The record reports a negotiated partition and names both parties to it, including the criminal one: "we made a treaty with the Lamanites and the robbers of Gadianton." Verse 29 gives the boundary as a landmark rather than a distance, "even to the narrow passage which led into the land southward." The same feature is used to fix a city at Ether 10:20, "by the narrow neck of land, by the place where the sea divides the land." A treaty is the only instrument in these books that assigns the whole continent between two powers, and it is dated to a single year, the three hundred and fiftieth.

chapter.title: The reason for his command is physical
chapter.text: Verse 1 names his stature. Nothing about his visitation in Mormon 1:15 is mentioned to the people.

chapter.title: He records a wrong guess about his own people
chapter.text: Verses 12 and 13 have him hope and then correct himself. The chapter leaves the mistake on the page.

chapter.title: Two kinds of sorrow are separated
chapter.text: Verse 13 distinguishes repentance from the sorrowing of the damned. 2 Corinthians 7:10 draws the same line.

chapter.title: The despair is specific
chapter.text: Verse 14 has them curse God, wish to die, and still fight for their lives. All three at once.

chapter.title: A phrase is coined for the verdict
chapter.text: Verse 15 gives the day of grace as past. The record uses that phrase nowhere else.

chapter.title: He tells you he is holding back
chapter.text: Verse 18 says the full account is elsewhere. The abridgment declares its own editing.

chapter.title: Winning and being abandoned happen together
chapter.text: Verses 25 and 26 have them rout an army larger than their own, and then record that the Lord's strength had left them.

chapter.title: The chapter closes on a border
chapter.text: Verse 29 divides the land at the narrow passage. What began as a retreat ends as a line on a map.

applications.title: Being picked for a thin reason still leaves you the job
applications.text: The people of Nephi appointed Mormon to lead their armies because he was young and large in stature. The criterion was poor and the assignment was real, which is a situation most people meet sooner or later.

applications.title: Write down the hope that did not pan out
applications.text: Mormon recorded rejoicing he later had to retract. An honest account keeps the wrong guesses.

applications.title: Check what your sorrow is about
applications.text: Grief over losing the pleasure is not grief over the sin. The chapter makes that the whole difference.

applications.title: Do the errand you were given years ago
applications.text: When the retreat reached Jashon, Mormon went according to the word of Ammaron and took the plates of Nephi. An instruction received at ten was carried out at twenty-four, in the middle of a rout.

applications.title: Say what you are leaving out
applications.text: He named the fuller record and where it went. Selection stated is not the same as selection hidden.

applications.title: A long sorrow is not despair
applications.text: Mormon says that sorrow has filled him all his days, and in the same sentence that he knows he shall be lifted up at the last day. Both clauses stand, and neither one cancels the other.

applications.title: Tell people what they are actually defending
applications.text: Mormon urged them to stand for their families and their own roofs, naming each in turn, and the next verse reports that it roused them somewhat. General appeals move nobody, and a list of particular things a person would lose does.

applications.title: Do not read the win as approval
applications.text: They beat an army half again their size and the Spirit was not with them. Outcomes are poor evidence of standing.

questions.text: What in my life has turned over completely?
What can I not seem to hold on to?
Is my regret about the sin or about the consequence?
When have I been angry at God and still fought to live?
What have I looked at so long that I have stopped describing it?
Whose words last roused me to stand?
Where have I succeeded without help I should have had?
